description: A folder tree of ordinary video files - phone clips, GoPro/action-cam footage, downloaded videos, anything with no dashcam-specific metadata at all. Meant to be a real, usable input source in its own right (not just a proof that the adapter boundary works), so the pipeline still produces something useful: a listing, gap-based trip grouping by timestamp, transcripts/translations/subtitles/scene descriptions via bv-generate/bv-scribe (those work off any video's own audio/frames, not off BlackVue conventions). See docs/CAMERA_ADAPTERS.md's 'What breaks' section for what's deliberately not offered, and unsupported_notes below for why.
unsupported_notes: No GPS: no map.mp4, no GPX export, no --movement trip bridging. Trip splitting still works on timestamp gaps alone. The archive detail page's start/stop location link and reverse geocoding still work per-recording when a photo carries an EXIF GPS tag or a video carries its own ISO 6709 container `location` tag - just no continuous real telemetry track for the trip as a whole.
No g-sensor: no gsensor.mp4/gsensor_graph.mp4, no --stitch-gsensor panel.
No multi-direction video: no --stitch camera-layout compositor, no rearview_mirror layout - export is a single-track passthrough of whichever video file each recording is.
No config.ini equivalent: trip gap threshold always uses default_trip_gap_seconds (300s) instead of a per-camera auto-derived nominal segment length.
No Event/Manual/Parking distinction: no --mode filtering, no --include-parking skip-and-replace, no max_parking_duration cap - every file is just 'a video'.
No live camera connection: bv-download, bv-config's endpoint setup, bv-gps, and bv-live are not applicable to this adapter and shouldn't be offered for it.

Thumbnails are generated via an ffmpeg frame-grab, not read from a camera-native .thm sidecar - either proactively by bv-generate --thumbnail (a normal, permanent archive asset once written, same as .aac/.duration.txt) or, if that hasn't been run yet, on first view in bv-web, which writes the same permanent file so later views are instant.

Timestamp comes from ffprobe's embedded creation_time metadata, falling back to file mtime if that's missing or looks wrong (e.g. reset by a file copy) - less reliable than BlackVue's own filename-embedded timestamp, so trip boundaries may be slightly off for files with bad/missing metadata.
